extra.message: The exception handler returns str(exc) and exc.__class__.__name__ to the client. The RuntimeError message includes the absolute server filesystem path BASE_EXPORT_DIR, leaking internal directory structure and implementation details to any caller that passes the internal-token gate.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: logger.warning writes the raw compensation intake request body and the value of the Authorization header to the application logs. Credentials and sensitive payroll data are persisted to log files that may be accessible to broader audiences than the application itself.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: redirect(next_url) uses the unvalidated 'lane' query parameter as the redirect target. An attacker who can pass the internal-token gate can redirect users to an arbitrary external URL, enabling phishing and token theft via a malicious site.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: pickle.loads(raw) deserializes attacker-controlled input taken from request.body (or the 'blob' GET parameter, optionally base64-decoded). pickle.loads can execute arbitrary code during unpickling, leading to remote code execution.

The 'ref' GET parameter is interpolated directly into BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json" with no sanitization, then the file is created and written. A value containing traversal sequences (e.g. ../../) allows writing arbitrary files outside the intended export directory, and the written content includes SSN/card data supplied by the caller.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: eval(expr, ...) executes the user-supplied 'expr' GET parameter. Restricting __builtins__ does not make eval safe: class/introspection gadgets (e.g. via ()['class'] chains) can escape the sandbox and achieve arbitrary code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: response.set_cookie("portal_crumb", marker) sets a cookie using a user-controlled value without Secure, HttpOnly, or SameSite attributes. The cookie is transmitted over plain HTTP and is accessible to JavaScript, and its value is fully attacker-controlled.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: urllib.request.urlopen(endpoint) fetches the user-supplied 'endpoint' GET parameter with no scheme or host allow-listing. This enables server-side request forgery against internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ metadata endpoints) and the response body is returned to the caller.

known = {"north": "4812", "south": "5930"} embeds verification secrets directly in source code and uses them to authorize access. Anyone with source access (or who guesses the short numeric values) can pass the verifier check; additionally the 404/403 split allows handle enumeration.

The Origin request header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to "true". This permissive CORS policy allows any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests and read the responses.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to "0" and clears Content-Security-Policy, disabling two core browser-side defenses for the response.

Template("Result: " + fragment).render() builds a Jinja2 template from the user-supplied 'fragment' GET parameter and renders it, then returns the output as text/html. This is a server-side template injection allowing arbitrary expression evaluation and code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The 'name' GET parameter is joined directly into BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name and request.body is written to that path. Traversal sequences in 'name' allow writing attacker-controlled content to arbitrary filesystem locations outside the export directory, enabling arbitrary file creation/overwrite.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The generated code/nonce is produced with the random module (random.choice), which is not cryptographically secure. Security-sensitive tokens must use secrets.SystemRandom or secrets.token_urlsafe; predictable nonces can be brute-forced.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False) is used to parse request.body via etree.fromstring. External entities and DTDs are resolved, enabling XXE attacks such as local file disclosure, denial of service via entity expansion, and SSRF.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The elevated access lane is granted solely because the ops_badge cookie or x-ops-badge header equals "lead". These values are entirely client-controlled, so any caller can set the cookie/header to "lead" to obtain elevated privileges without any server-side identity verification.

cwe: CWE-565: Reliance on Cookies without Validation

extra.message: MongoClient(...).ops.records.find_one(query) is called with query taken directly from the parsed JSON body (payload.get('filter', payload)). An attacker can supply MongoDB operator injection (e.g. {"$where": ...}, {"$ne": null}) to manipulate the query and extract or bypass intended filters.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: ssl._create_unverified_context() disables peer certificate verification for the outbound HTTPS request, allowing man-in-the-middle attackers to impersonate the partner endpoint and intercept or alter the connection.

SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded value "dev-only-change-me" when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset. Because this default is committed to the repository, anyone can forge signed session cookies and CSRF tokens, bypassing authentication if the application is deployed without setting the environment variable.

DEBUG defaults to True when DJANGO_DEBUG is unset. Running with DEBUG=True in production exposes detailed stack traces and the full settings (including SECRET_KEY and database credentials) on error pages, leaking sensitive information.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: default_db embeds the database credentials postgres:postgres directly in source code. These hardcoded credentials are disclosed with the source and used as the fallback database URL.

SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE and CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE are never set (they default to False) even though SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY and CSRF_COOKIE_HTTPONLY are enabled. Without the Secure attribute, session and CSRF cookies are transmitted over unencrypted HTTP, exposing them to network interception.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The "reject" branch only checks role in {HR_ADMIN, MANAGER} and the compensation status; unlike the "manager_approve" branch it does not verify comp.employee.manager == request.user.employee_profile. Any manager can therefore reject compensation requests for employees who are not their direct reports, an unauthorized state change to a sensitive compensation workflow.

Imported employee accounts are created with user.set_password("ChangeMe123!"), a single well-known hardcoded password applied to every imported user. Until each user changes it, any attacker who knows this value can authenticate as any imported employee.

DEMO_PASSWORD = "DemoPass123!" is hardcoded in source and used to create every seeded demo account. The credential is committed to the repository and is therefore known to anyone with access to the code, enabling login to all demo accounts.
